headline: Zuckerberg predicts billions will have personal AI agents in five years, driving Meta's next wave of products
summary: Mark Zuckerberg outlined a future where billions use personal AI agents for finance, health, and daily tasks, positioning Meta's messaging platforms as central to this shift.
details: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that billions of people will have their own personal AI agents within the next five years. He shared this vision during the company's recent quarterly earnings call with investors.

These AI agents are envisioned to understand user goals and work 24/7 on their behalf across various domains. Zuckerberg suggested applications in personal finance, health management, interpersonal relationships, and household tasks.

He emphasized that Meta's messaging platforms, particularly WhatsApp, will become increasingly important as users interact with multiple agents. WhatsApp is already the leading platform for Meta AI interactions.
Meta is not alone in pursuing agentic AI; Google has integrated custom AI agents into its Search, and Anthropic's Claude Code assistant has seen a surge in subscriptions.

Despite this ambitious vision, Meta's stock dropped almost 10% after its latest earnings report. The company's Reality Labs division continues to incur significant losses, totaling around $88 billion since 2021.
Meta's AI investments are also escalating, contributing to a 91% year-over-year drop in free cash flow this quarter. The company recently partnered with BlackRock to build a $14 billion data center.

Zuckerberg believes these personal agents will form the foundation for Meta's next wave of products and revenue lines. While business agents have seen adoption, the challenge lies in scaling consumer AI agents to billions.

headline: Microsoft confirms Copilot ‘super app’ coming this year
summary: The upcoming app will merge Copilot’s chat, coding, and agentic features, spanning both consumer and commercial experiences.
details: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella confirmed during an earnings call that an AI "super app" combining Copilot's chat, coding, and agentic capabilities is launching this year. It will cater to both consumer and commercial users.
Nadella stated that Copilot is rapidly evolving, bringing together these experiences, including code, into one unified application. He called this a major step forward and promised more details soon.

This confirmation follows a Fortune report months ago about Microsoft's plans for a super app blending Copilot chatbot, GitHub Copilot, Copilot Cowork, and its Autopilot system. OpenAI also recently unveiled its ChatGPT Work app with similar integrations.
Microsoft's revenue surged to $90 billion last quarter, primarily driven by its strong performance in AI and cloud businesses, highlighting the company's focus on AI integration.
